# Candidate crystals
- Crystal-K2: inorganic scintillator, high light yield, fast decay.
- Crystal-K1: inorganic scintillator, medium light yield.
- Crystal-K3: inorganic scintillator, mature growth process, lower light yield.
All three are available in the required sizes from at least one vendor.

# Earlier simulation summary (2025, nominal 5 cm thickness)
Energy resolution at 662 keV (FWHM): Crystal-K2 2.9%, Crystal-K1 4.5%, Crystal-K3 8.5%.
Thickness dependence was weak in the 3-8 cm range.

# Meeting notes 2026-02-11
Attendees discussed the shielding upgrade (lead + copper, complete) and the schedule for commissioning in Q3. Action: finalise the crystal choice this quarter.

# Radiopurity assay campaign, Q1 2026
Sample crystals of each candidate were counted for 30 days in the underground HPGe station.
Intrinsic background of the crystal, 100-3000 keV (counts/kg/day):
- Crystal-K2: 2.0 +- 0.2   (dominated by internal contamination of the crystal itself)
- Crystal-K1: 0.30 +- 0.05
- Crystal-K3: 0.10 +- 0.03
Facility background budget for the spectrometer crystal: 0.5 counts/kg/day.
Contact: radiopurity working group.

# Shielding status
The 20 cm lead + 5 cm OFHC copper castle is installed. Radon purge with boil-off nitrogen is operational.

# DAQ readout plan
The PMT signal is digitised at 250 MS/s with 14-bit ADCs. Firmware supports pulse-shape discrimination. No change is needed for any crystal candidate.

# Schedule
Q2: crystal procurement. Q3: assembly and commissioning. Q4: first assays.

input.justification:
Crystal-K2 has the best simulated resolution (2.9% FWHM at 662 keV) but its intrinsic background from the Q1 2026 assay is 2.0 ± 0.2 counts/kg/day (internal contamination), about four times the 0.5 counts/kg/day hard limit, so it is excluded. Crystal-K3 has the lowest background (0.10 ± 0.03) but its simulated resolution is 8.5%, much worse than K1. Crystal-K1 meets the background limit (0.30 ± 0.05 counts/kg/day, with margin to 0.5) and gives 4.5% FWHM at 662 keV, the best resolution among the compliant candidates. The 2025 simulation reports only weak thickness dependence over 3–8 cm, so I kept the nominal 5 cm, which is the thickness the simulated resolution was computed for and which lies within the 2–10 cm constraint. Caveat: the only resolution figures available are from the 2025 simulation at nominal 5 cm; I did not run a new thickness scan, so the 4.5% value at 5 cm is not verified for other thicknesses. The 4.5% figure is also a simulation result, not a measurement.</justification>
